newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel has no proof on Arafat "green light".
newsitem.headline: Israel has no proof on Arafat "green light".

text.p: Israel has no proof Palestinian President Yasser Arafat gave a green light to Moslem militants to attack the Jewish state, a senior Israeli army officer said on Tuesday.

"We have no information or clearcut evidence that Arafat gave the green light," Israel's parliament spokesman, briefing reporters, quoted a senior military intelligence officer as telling the Knesset's Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee.
"But his style, language and body language were understood by terror groups to have given the go-ahead," the officer said.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday the Palestinian Authority led by Arafat gave the green light for a suicide bombing that killed three Israeli women in a Tel Aviv cafe on Friday.

"Every time there is an impasse or they have a grievance against us they send terrorists," Netanyahu said on ABC television's "This Week." "In this case they were sent a green light from the Palestinian Authority. On this we have absolute information."

Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, asked on the CBS programme "Face the Nation" on Sunday if Arafat had given a "green light" for violence, said: "There is clearly perception of the green light but no concrete evidence."

Israeli-Palestinian relations have been in crisis since Israel broke ground on a 6,500-home new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18. The bombing on Friday pushed contacts to the breaking point.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu and Arafat left the door open to a summit meeting to iron out differences but each set conditions, underscoring the crisis.
